Summary (for narrative):
- Deployment modes: Hosted (default), Dedicated (customer‑pinned GPU pool with VPC peering), Private (customer‑managed VPC or on‑prem with private control plane).
- Isolation model: Tenants are separated at three layers: (1) model runtime isolation via per‑tenant serving pools and per‑tenant GPU pools in Dedicated; (2) network isolation via subnet/VPC segmentation and Security Group policies; (3) control plane logical tenancy that enforces RBAC and mTLS for service‑to‑service communication.
- Control plane vs data plane: Control plane (API control, model routing, billing) flows through a private control plane in Private deployments; it is accessible only from customer‑registered management CIDRs and authenticated via mutual TLS. Data plane (inference traffic) traverses customer VPC or dedicated egress gateways; we avoid cross‑tenant hairpinning.
- Egress enforcement: Each tenant in Dedicated/Private has a tenancy label enforced at the egress gateway. Outbound requests are funneled through a centralized proxy that enforces allowlists per tenant. For Private on‑prem customers using customer KMS, egress is entirely under customer control or optionally routed through a Redwood NAT with restricted ACLs.
- KMS boundaries: For Private deployments, customer key material never leaves the customer KMS (HSM/KMS pull model). For Dedicated, we provide dedicated KMS keys scoped to the customer account with strict IAM and audit logging.
- Evidence locations (examples): drive:/redwood/evidence/secure-arch/evergreen/diagram_v1, jira:SEC-4829, soc2:/control-test-extracts/segmentation_2026Q4.xlsx

Attached: control-plane-dataflow.pdf (redacted for external), soc2-control-test-summary.xlsx (redaction applied).

Jordan — delivering the initial packet per the plan. Attachments included with this email: blast-radius-diagram-v1.png, segmented-egress-matrix.csv.

Quick answers inline below to help reviewers:
1) KMS model (concise): For Private deployments where the customer provides KMS/HSM, Redwood operates in a pull model and never stores unencrypted key material. Cryptographic operations that require the private key occur inside the customer‑managed KMS/HSM. For Dedicated (Redwood‑managed infra) we provision a customer‑scoped key in Redwood's KMS; key material is protected by HSM and access is restricted to a small set of provisioning services via strict IAM and mutual TLS; remote unwrapping by Redwood personnel is not permitted without a documented and auditable emergency rotation workflow.

2) Egress example (concise): Tenant A inference call -> local tenant subnet -> egress gateway (10.32.14.7) -> tenant proxy (port 3128) -> outbound allowlist lookup -> external API 52.45.112.9:443. Outbound packets are tagged with tenant label; gateway enforces per‑tenant ACLs and logs at the proxy layer. We include a sample row in segmented-egress-matrix.csv demonstrating this flow.

SOC 2 excerpt: We've redacted PII but included control IDs and pass rows. See soc2-control-test-summary.xlsx in the evidence bundle (drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A_example_drive_link).

Next steps: Stephanie will do a final text pass; we will upload the full control-plane-dataflow.pdf and the cleaned SIG/CAIQ mapping to the drive by Jan 22.
